facebook.long_form:
Carlos Alcaraz is back in another Japan Open semifinal — and this time, he's set for something tennis rarely sees on the ATP Tour: an all-Spanish showdown.

Alcaraz advanced from the quarterfinals on Sunday after Denis Shapovalov, who had pushed him to a tiebreak in a tense first set, was forced to retire with an upper right thigh injury while trailing 2-1 in the second set. Alcaraz had just won the tiebreak 7-3 when Shapovalov's body gave out. The defending champion moved into his spot in the semifinals without breaking a sweat after the set.

On the other side of the bracket, Jaume Munar had no such drama — the Spaniard from Mallorca rolled past Frenchman Kyrian Jacquet 6-4, 6-2 to set up the Spanish clash. Meanwhile, No. 2 seed Arthur Fils was shocked by Monégasque qualifier Valentin Vacherot, one of the surprise stories of this Japan Open week.

Monday's semifinal lineup: Alcaraz vs. Munar — Alcaraz leads the H2H 3-1 but Munar has been quietly building one of the more impressive weeks of his career. On the other side, Vacherot faces the fourth semifinalist.

Alcaraz is 7-0 all-time in Tokyo and defending his 2025 title. Anything less than a final appearance would be a surprise. Who are you rooting for?

---
